To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a novel fusion protein composed of a tumor-specific antibody fused to a major histocompatibility complex (MHCI) molecule associated with an antigenic peptide that redirects CMV-specific T-cell immunity to eliminate tumor cells.

a novel generation of tumor antigen–specific fusion proteins consisting of a full immunoglobulin molecule connected to a single pMHCI complex can redirect a highly functional, differentiated subset of CMV- specific T cells to eliminate antigen-expressing tumor cells.

a novel generation of tumor antigen–peptide–major histocompatibility class–antibody (pMHCI) fusion proteins selectively engage antigen-specific cytotoxic T lymphocyte populations to eliminate tumor cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel cancer therapies that are based on the use of virus-derived peptides presented by major histocompatibility complex class I (pMHCI) molecules.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of cancer.
the development of novel cancer immunotherapeutics that are based on the redirection of the cytolytic immune response to tumor cells by the use of bifunctional antibodies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pMHCI–lgGs represent a novel class of tumor-specific immunotherapeutics that selectively engage antigen-specific effector CD8+ T lymphocytes and redirect their cytotoxic activity to tumor cells.

this study shows that a new type of fusion protein, consisting of a tumor antigen-specific full immunoglobulin and a single major histo-compatibility class I complex (pMHCI-IgG), can be used to redirect a subset of cytomegaloviruses (CMV)-reactive T cells to tumor cells, which are then eliminated.
the fusion protein described in this paper has the potential to redirect CMV-specific CD8+T cells to tumor cells, and this could be used to treat patients with CMV-specific CD4+T cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a novel generation for the redirection of T-cell effector function by using the full immunoglobulin as the targeting unit.
we developed a novel class of fusion proteins that selectively redirect a naturally occurring population of cytotoxic T cells in humans to eliminate tumor cells in a non–antigen-specific manner.
we developed an entirely novel class of anticance immunotherapeutics, which we called bifunctional MHCI antibody fusion molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have shown for the first time that a fusion protein consisting of a tumor-specific peptide-MHC class I complex connected to an antibody is able to redirect a naturally occurring population of CMV-specific cytotoxic T cells against tumor cells.
we developed a novel fusion protein that can redirect the cytomegalovirusspecific T cells to kill tumor cells.

a subset of human CD8 T cells that are highly functional and specific for a single virus, CMV, can be redirected to tumor cells by using a novel class of fusion proteins that contain a tumor antigen–derived peptide presented on major histocompatibility complex (MHCI) class I and a full immunoglobulin (IgG).
